title: FERC Compliance Directives — Docket P-401-000: Letter to American Electric Power discussing the 06/02/2026 Dam Safety Inspection et al. for the Mottville Hydroelectric Project under P-401.
text:
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION
Office of Energy Projects
Division of Dam Safety and Inspections
Chicago Regional Office
In reply refer to: P-0401
July 2, 2026
VIA Electronic Mail
Mr. Gene F. Sirca, Jr., Ph.D., P.E., S.E.
Chief Hydro Dam Safety Engineer
American Electric Power
gfsirca@aep.com
Re: Mottville Hydroelectric Project, FERC No. 401
- 2026 Dam Safety Inspection (DSI) Follow-up
- 2025 Dam Safety Surveillance and Monitoring Report (DSSMR)
- Public Safety Plan (PSP) Revision
Dear Mr. Sirca:
The 2026 Dam Safety Inspection of Mottville Hydroelectric Project, FERC
No. 401 was conducted on June 2, 2026 by Mr. Eduardo Prieto, P.E. of the FERC
Chicago Regional Office. He was accompanied by Mses. Justine Penix and Jodi Slough,
and Messrs. Rich Walag, Erwin Supranata, Rob Beller, Craig Bonesteel and yourself of
American Electric Power (AEP). Based on our inspection, it was concluded that no
immediate dam safety-related items need to be addressed. Be advised that we may
provide you with comments that develop as a result of our preparation of the dam safety
inspection report.
The 2025 Dam Safety Surveillance and Monitoring Report (DSSMR) by AEP
was received May 28, 2026, and was reviewed following the inspection. The FERC’s
review comments are listed below and should be addressed with the next annual (2026)
DSSMR submittal due by April 1, 2027.
• The DSSMR notes that Indiana Michigan Power Company (IMPC) plans to
complete erosion repair and riprap replacement at the right embankment in 2026
and will also address the damaged drainpipes. Please provide a status update in
your next DSSMR submittal.
• The DSSMR notes that IMPC plans to closely monitor the water levels in
Spillway Pier Wells 1, 2, 6, and 7 in 2026 and include the evaluation in the 2026
DSSMR, due April 1, 2027. The well information and data will also be evaluated
during the 2027 Part 12D Periodic Inspection to determine whether further

maintenance, replacement, abandonment or installation of new well(s) or
piezometers is warranted. This is acceptable.
The DSSMR includes a statement from the Chief Dam Safety Engineer that the dam
is safe for continued operation. Our review finds that the 2025 DSSMR fulfills the
requirements in Chapter 14 – Appendix K of our Engineering Guidelines. The 2026
DSSMR is due by April 1, 2027.
Our records indicated that the Public Safety Plan (PSP) for the Mottville project
was filed on January 13, 2015, and is more than 10 years old. Consistent with the
Commission’s public safety guidelines and standard dam safety practices, Public Safety
Plans older than ten years must be reviewed, updated, and resubmitted to ensure that
public safety measures reflect current site conditions and operational practices.
In accordance with 18 CFR § 12.52, it is your responsibility to take all reasonable
measures to maintain and operate your hydropower project in a manner that is safe for the
public. As part of this update, you should reassess potential public safety hazards
associated with the project and evaluate the adequacy of existing safety measures. Any
additional measures necessary to protect the public should be identified and put into place
as appropriate.
The Public Safety Plan should be updated and filed to this office by December 31,
2026. Further details regarding Public Safety are available at
https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-04/public-safety.pdf
You may contact Mr. Eduardo Prieto at (312) 596-4449
(Eduardo.Prieto@ferc.gov) or me at (312) 596-4456 or if you have questions.
Sincerely,
Marilyn Sabido, P.E.
Regional Engineer
